cases.sentence: I am ate an apple yesterday.
cases.tree: Provisional B-R working tree. Some groupings could not be analyzed confidently.
cases.explanation:
Partial grammatical analysis. The findings below are supported by available evidence.

‘ate’ is a simple past form. Auxiliary ‘am’ takes an -ing form in the progressive or a past participle in the passive.

If you intend the simple past, one possible revision is “I ate an apple yesterday.”

cases.explanation:
Partial grammatical analysis. The findings below are supported by available evidence.

‘If’ introduces a conditional clause. It can work as a fragment in conversation. In formal writing, it needs a main clause to make a complete sentence.

Write ‘dont’ as ‘don't’ to mark the negative contraction. ‘do’ is the auxiliary, ‘n’t’ marks negation, and ‘know’ is the lexical verb in its plain form after the auxiliary.
